findings: Twenty-four project-authored B1 cases fit the first-evidence window but support directional screening, not production-quality claims or fine-grained slice conclusions.
A program-specific schema is needed because the shared channel enum cannot represent all contract genres without a premature shared-infrastructure change.

Free-form required facts and forbidden claims are too brittle for adversarial fidelity; expected values need structured aliases for numbers, dates, names, attribution, polarity, caveats, and placeholders.
Revision cases need explicit preservation spans and edit budgets to measure minimality, overcompression, and unnecessary rewriting.
Project-authored provenance, rights status, task family, adversarial features, topic, and time-lineage fields are required for honest split and slice handling.
Approximately half the cases should carry cross-cutting fidelity traps because factual fidelity has the largest development-score weight.
accepted_schema_findings: program-level task family and extended genre/channel vocabulary
structured expected facts and forbidden assertions
revision edit budgets and preservation spans
accepted_deterministic_checks: number, unit, date, name, and attribution preservation
subject, heading, and call-to-action format checks
risks: The small benchmark has low statistical power and cannot establish publish readiness.
Lexical deterministic checks can reject valid paraphrases or miss semantic errors.
Frequent B1 item-level feedback invites overfitting, so B2 cadence must be preregistered.
Ox Alpha must not author the cases or act as candidate and sole judge on this benchmark.
All case material must remain genuinely project-authored and free of third-party personal data.
One existing active profile cannot establish multi-profile controllability.

uncertainties: Exact edit-budget thresholds require preregistration before inspecting comparative results.
Multi-profile slice sizing remains provisional until descriptive profile specifications exist.
